correctness.rationale: For the repaired vector statement in repairs/5/RESULT.md, take windows of lengths u≤v with u+v<N; there are v−u+1 containing shifts and two shifts at each overlap u−r for 1≤r<u. Common signs cancel, giving the stated finite covariance after subtracting the product of means at each overlapping shift. The geometric tail gives C with d=|h_i−h_j|, and the last term (u+v−1)mu^(u+v) vanishes. For each linear combination, the absolute covariance sum is uniformly bounded by the same overlap count and a convergent geometric series. Keeping blocks of size floor(N^(1/3)) separated by gaps of length O(log N) (including at wraparound) retains independent block sums with maximum size o(sqrt N). The o(N) omitted terms have o(N) variance; the retained variance converges to the asserted quadratic form after normalization. Lindeberg–Feller and Cramér–Wold apply, with zero limiting variance handled by Chebyshev. The exact mean gives the phase-dependent vector shift, and the positive marginal variances ensure Gaussian orthants have null boundary. The original scalar assertions are mathematically sound but were already covered. Frozen VERIFICATION.md and verify_kac.py were inspected, not rerun; finite checks do not establish this CLT.

evidence: Scalar normal limits plus convergence of covariances do not entail a joint Gaussian limit. To apply Cramér–Wold, combinations of products from several lengths must be handled at once.
The overlap bound and block construction handle those combinations uniformly; the resulting kernel retains both the d term and the geometric contribution.

value.rationale: The repaired claim identifies correlations between different nearby times at the relaxation scale in one static environment. Those correlations determine simultaneous sign probabilities and give information unavailable from the known scalar CLT or the signal-to-noise timescale alone. The uniform growing-window proof is needed to justify using the explicit kernel as a joint Gaussian law.
